Description: In runes mode only variables declared with $state are reactive. Arrays and plain objects become deeply reactive proxies, so mutations such as array.push trigger updates. Implicit `let` reactivity and the assignment-only rule belong to legacy (Svelte 4) components.
Do: let count = $state(0); mutate $state arrays and objects directly
Don't: Rely on a plain let being reactive in a runes-mode component
Code Good: let count = $state(0); let todos = $state([]); todos.push({ text, done: false });
Code Bad: let count = 0; // not reactive in runes mode

Description: $derived replaces `$:` derivations: the value re-computes when the state it reads changes. Use $derived.by(() => { ... }) when the derivation needs several statements. Do not copy values into other state from an effect.
Don't: Assign derived values from $effect or use $: in runes mode

Description: $effect runs in the browser after mount and again when state it read synchronously changes; return a function to clean up. Effects never run during server-side rendering. The docs describe $effect as an escape hatch for things like analytics, third-party libraries and direct DOM work, and advise against using it to synchronize state.
Do: Use $effect for external side effects and return a cleanup function
Don't: Use $effect to keep one piece of state in sync with another
Code Good: $effect(() => { const id = setInterval(tick, interval); return () => clearInterval(id); });

Description: Destructure props from $props() with fallback values; `export let` is legacy Svelte 4 syntax. Rename reserved names with property renaming and collect the remaining props with a rest element, which replaces $$props and $$restProps.
Don't: export let in runes mode, or $$props / $$restProps
Code Good: let { name, count = 0, class: klass, ...rest } = $props(); // <div class={klass} {...rest}>
Code Bad: export let name; export let count = 0; // <div {...$$restProps}>

Guideline: Do not mutate props; use callbacks or $bindable
Description: Props should not be mutated unless they are declared with $bindable. Communicate changes to the parent with callback props, or declare a bindable prop when parent and child must share the value through bind:.
Do: Call a callback prop or declare $bindable() for two-way binding
Don't: Assign to or mutate a non-bindable prop inside the child
Code Bad: let { items } = $props(); items.push(next); // mutating a non-bindable prop

Guideline: Type props with an interface on $props
Description: Annotate the destructured $props() with an interface; Svelte 4's $$Props interface is legacy. Type callback props as functions and snippets with the Snippet type.
Don't: interface $$Props in runes mode
Code Good: interface Props { name: string; onsave?: (data: Data) => void } let { name, onsave }: Props = $props();
Code Bad: interface $$Props { name: string } export let name: string;

Description: Simplified input handling
Don't: oninput with manual assignment

Description: Reference DOM nodes
Don't: querySelector in onMount

Guideline: Use event attributes, not on: directives
Description: In Svelte 5 event handlers are ordinary attributes and props such as onclick. Modifiers like |preventDefault work only with the legacy on: directive, so call event.preventDefault() inside the handler. Forward a handler by passing the prop through or spreading rest props.
Do: onclick={handler}; call e.preventDefault() in the handler
Don't: on:click or on:submit|preventDefault in runes mode

Description: createEventDispatcher is deprecated in Svelte 5. Components accept callback props instead, which are typed like any other prop.
Do: Accept a callback prop and call it
Don't: createEventDispatcher and dispatch for component events

Guideline: onMount runs only in the browser
Description: onMount runs after the component mounts and never during server-side rendering; a function returned from it runs on unmount. Component script code also runs on the server, so browser-only setup belongs in onMount or $effect.
Do: Put browser-only setup in onMount and return its cleanup
Don't: Start timers or touch window and document in the script body
Code Good: onMount(() => { const id = setInterval(tick, interval); return () => clearInterval(id); });
Code Bad: const id = setInterval(tick, interval); // also runs during SSR and is never cleared

Description: beforeUpdate and afterUpdate are disallowed in runes mode. Use $effect.pre for work before the DOM updates and $effect for work after it.
Don't: beforeUpdate or afterUpdate in runes mode
Code Good: $effect.pre(() => { messages.length; /* runs before the DOM updates */ });

Guideline: Share state from .svelte.js modules; keep stores for streams
Description: With runes, cross-component state and extracted logic can live in .svelte.js or .svelte.ts modules using $state; runes are not compiled in plain .js files. Stores remain a good fit for complex asynchronous streams or manual control over updates; in components the $ prefix subscribes and unsubscribes automatically, while manual subscribe calls need an unsubscribe.
Do: Export $state objects from a .svelte.js module and mutate their properties
Don't: Use runes in plain .js files or leave manual store subscriptions open
Code Good: // state.svelte.js: export const user = $state({ name: '' }); // Component: import { user } from './state.svelte.js'; user.name = input;
Code Bad: // state.js: export const user = $state({ name: '' }); // runes are not compiled in plain .js files

Description: Slots are deprecated in Svelte 5. Content between a component's tags becomes the children snippet; named content areas are snippet props rendered with {@render}. Use {@render name?.()} or {#if name} for optional snippets instead of $$slots.
Do: Render children and named snippet props with {@render}
Don't: <slot>, named slots or $$slots in runes mode
Code Good: let { header, children } = $props(); {@render header?.()} {@render children?.()}

Description: Snippets take parameters, which replace slot props and let:. Type snippet props with the Snippet type from 'svelte', for example Snippet<[Entry]>.
Do: Declare {#snippet item(entry)} in the parent and call {@render item(entry)} in the child
Don't: Slot props with let: in runes mode

Description: A component's <style> is scoped to that component by default. :global(...) and :global {} blocks escape scoping for third-party markup or document-level rules.
Do: Keep component styles scoped; use :global(...) only for content the component does not own
Don't: Make all component styles global

Description: Svelte's transition directives (fade, fly, slide and others from svelte/transition) handle enter and exit for conditional blocks.
Don't: CSS classes for exit animations on {#if} content
Code Bad:
{#if visible}
...
{/if} // removed immediately; a CSS exit transition never plays

Description: Since Svelte 4 transitions are local: they play only when their own block is created or destroyed, not when parent blocks change. The |local modifier is legacy; add |global to opt into playing on parent block changes.
Do: Rely on the local default; add |global only when parent changes should animate
Don't: Add |local (redundant) or expect parent block changes to run local transitions

Description: Svelte transitions are driven by the Web Animations API rather than CSS, so a global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule that zeroes transition and animation durations does not affect them. Read prefersReducedMotion from svelte/motion (5.7+) and adjust the transition parameters.
Do: Use prefersReducedMotion.current to reduce or remove transition movement
Don't: Rely on a global CSS reduced-motion rule to stop Svelte transitions
Code Good: import { prefersReducedMotion } from 'svelte/motion';
Code Bad: /* @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { transition-duration: 0s !important; } } — does not affect Svelte transitions */

Guideline: Prefer attachments for reusable DOM behavior
Description: use: actions still work, but since Svelte 5.29 attachments ({@attach fn}) are the more flexible alternative. An attachment receives the element, re-runs when reactive state it reads changes, and may return a cleanup function that runs before re-running or after the element is removed.
Do: {@attach fn} for reusable element behavior with cleanup
Don't: Query the DOM in onMount for every element that needs the behavior
Code Good: <div {@attach (node) => { const t = tooltip(node, text); return () => t.destroy(); }}>

Description: Proper list reconciliation
Don't: Index as key or no key

Description: Handle async states
Don't: Manual promise handling

Description: Reset component state
Don't: Manual destroy/create
Code Bad: Manually unmounting and recreating a component to reset its state

Description: $state.raw opts out of deep proxying: the value can only be reassigned, not mutated. It suits large arrays or objects that are replaced rather than edited. The immutable compiler option has no effect in runes mode.
Don't: Mutate $state.raw values or set the immutable option in runes mode
Code Bad: let rows = $state.raw(initialRows); rows.push(next); // no update <svelte:options immutable />

Description: Use interactive elements for interactive content. The compiler warns (a11y_click_events_have_key_events, a11y_no_static_element_interactions) when a static element such as <div> gets a click handler.
Don't: div for everything

Description: Accessible state changes
Don't: Silent dynamic updates

Description: File-based routing
Don't: Custom routing setup

Description: Load data before render
Don't: onMount for data fetching
Code Good: export async function load({ fetch, params }) { const res = await fetch(`/api/items/${params.id}`); return { item: await res.json() }; }

Description: Server-side data loading
Don't: +page.js for API keys

Description: Server-side form handling
Don't: API routes for forms
Code Good: export const actions = { default: async ({ request }) => { const data = await request.formData(); /* validate and save */ } };

Description: $app/state (added in SvelteKit 2.12) exposes page, navigating and updated as fine-grained runes-based state read without the $ prefix. $app/stores was deprecated in favor of it and removed in SvelteKit 3.
Do: import { page } from '$app/state' and read page.url, page.params, page.data
Don't: Import from $app/stores or parse window.location
Code Bad: import { page } from '$app/stores'; {$page.url.pathname} // removed in SvelteKit 3

Guideline: Check the SvelteKit major before applying config and aliases
Description: SvelteKit 3 no longer supports svelte.config.js: options move into the sveltekit() Vite plugin. The $lib alias is no longer generated; declare a #lib subpath import in package.json and include file extensions in those imports. Read the installed @sveltejs/kit version before copying conventions from SvelteKit 2 projects.
Do: Follow the installed major: in SvelteKit 3 use plugin options and #lib imports with extensions
Don't: Assume svelte.config.js and $lib exist in a SvelteKit 3 project
Code Bad: import { formatDate } from '$lib/format'; // alias not generated in SvelteKit 3
